parameters.name: DownloadProtocol
parameters.description:
The protocol used to download over-the-air update package. Valid values: **HTTPS** (default) and **MQTT**. After the device receives over-the-air update package download information pushed by IoT Platform, the device uses this protocol to download over-the-air update package.

><notice>To use the MQTT protocol to download update packages, the following conditions must be met:
- Supported regions: China (Shanghai), China (Beijing), and China (Shenzhen) only.
- OTA update package: contains only one file, and the file size does not exceed 16 MB.
- Device SDK: You must use the latest version of the C language Link SDK provided by IoT Platform to develop OTA update and MQTT file download capabilities. For more information, see [OTA update code sample for downloading update packages over MQTT](~~330985~~).

></notice>

parameters.name: FirmwareId
parameters.description:
The ID of the OTA upgrade package. This is the unique identifier of the upgrade package.

**FirmwareId** is one of the parameters returned when you call [CreateOTAFirmware](~~147311~~) to create an OTA upgrade package.

You can also call [ListOTAFirmware](~~147450~~) to obtain the ID from the response.

parameters.name: IotInstanceId
parameters.description:
The instance ID. You can view the **ID** of the current instance on the **Overview** page in the IoT Platform console.

><notice>
- If this parameter is available, you must specify this parameter. Otherwise, the call fails.
- If no <props="intl"><ph>**Overview** page or </ph></props>ID is available, you do not need to specify this parameter.

></notice>

For more information about instances, see [Overview](~~356505~~).

parameters.name: NeedConfirm
parameters.description:
Specifies whether device OTA upgrades require confirmation from a mobile app. You must develop the mobile app on your own.


- **false** (default): No confirmation is required. OTA upgrade task information is obtained based on the **NeedPush** parameter.
- **true**: Confirmation is required. The device cannot obtain OTA upgrade task information until the app confirms the OTA upgrade. Then, the device obtains OTA upgrade task information based on the **NeedPush** parameter.

parameters.name: NeedPush
parameters.description:
Specifies whether IoT Platform proactively pushes over-the-air update task to the device.

- **true** (default): IoT Platform proactively pushes over-the-air update task to online devices within over-the-air update scope after the batch task is created.
    
    In this case, the device can still proactively send a request to IoT Platform to obtain OTA update task information.

- **false**: The device must send a request to IoT Platform to obtain OTA update task information.

parameters.name: ProductKey
parameters.description: The ProductKey of the product to which the OTA upgrade package belongs.

sub_parameters.name: Key
sub_parameters.description:
The key of the batch tag. The key can contain only letters, digits, and periods (.). The key must be 1 to 30 characters in length. You can add up to 10 batch tags.

Batch tags are sent to the device when IoT Platform pushes the update notification to the device.

> Batch tags are optional. The **Required** field is set to **Yes** because if you specify a batch tag, you must specify both **Tag.N.Value** and **Tag.N.Key** as a pair.

sub_parameters.name: Value
sub_parameters.description:
The value of the batch tag. The value must be 1 to 1024 characters in length. You can add up to 10 batch tags. The total length of all batch tag keys and values cannot exceed 4096 characters.

> Batch tags are optional. The **Required** field is set to **Yes** because if you specify a batch tag, you must specify both **Tag.N.Value** and **Tag.N.Key** as a pair.

parameters.name: TargetDeviceName
parameters.description:
The devices to authenticate for the OTA upgrade.

> - The product to which the device belongs must be the same as the product to which the OTA upgrade package belongs.
- Device names cannot be duplicate.
- You can specify up to 10 device names.

parameters.name: TimeoutInMinutes
parameters.description: The timeout period for the device update. Unit: minutes. Valid values: 1 to 1440.
